title: Australia powers Allianz P&C earnings
full_text:
Australia powers Allianz P&C earnings
Allianz says its Australian property and casualty business made an operating profit of €254 million ($413 million) in the third quarter – the second-best result after Germany’s €342 million ($556 million).
For the nine months to September, the Australian P&C unit delivered an operating profit of €559 million ($909 million), up from €449 million ($730 million) a year earlier. Business volume grew to €4.517 billion ($7.35 billion) from €3.866 billion ($6.29 billion) and operating insurance revenue increased to €4.16 billion ($6.76 billion) from €3.54 billion ($5.75 billion).
At the group level, operating profit rose 6.2% to €4.7 billion ($7.64 billion) in the third quarter and 7.8% to a record €14.1 billion ($22.93 billion) in the nine months to September.
The P&C division’s third-quarter operating profit dropped 7.9% to €2.2 billion ($3.57 billion), but it gained 3.2% to €7.1 billion ($11.54 billion) in the nine-month period.
“Allianz’s record operating profit of €14.1 billion for the first nine months of 2026 reflects the disciplined execution of our strategy,” CEO Oliver Bate said.
“Yet we are not standing still: at a time when many people are finding protection and retirement solutions harder to afford, we are working to leverage our scale and expertise to deliver relevant, accessible solutions to our clients.”
Allianz has raised the upper end of its operating profit target range to €18.6 billion ($30.25 billion).
